children: Benitec Biopharma reported a net loss of $45.5 million for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared with a $37.9 million loss the prior year, and held $180.0 million in cash and cash equivalents at year-end. Total operating expenses were $51.2 million, driven by higher R&D and G&A costs, while other income, net, largely from interest income, partially offset operating losses. The company reiterated plans to initiate a pivotal trial for BB-301 in mid-2027 and will present interim Phase 1b/2a data at ESGCT in October 2026.
Total operating expenses: $51.2 million for the year ended June 30, 2026 (compared with $41.8 million in 2025).
Research and development expense: $23.4 million for FY2026 (up from $18.3 million in FY2025).
General and administrative expense: $27.8 million for FY2026 (up from $23.4 million in FY2025).
Net loss attributable to shareholders: $45.5 million, or $0.98 per basic and diluted share, for the year ended June 30, 2026 (prior year net loss $37.9 million, or $1.05 per share).
Cash and cash equivalents: $180.0 million as of June 30, 2026.
Clinical progress: All six Cohort 1 (low dose) patients completed 12-month follow-up and Cohort 2 (high dose) is fully enrolled with three patients treated without safety issues.
Regulatory engagement: Held a Type C meeting with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration in Q3 2026 to discuss pivotal study design; FDA meeting minutes expected in October 2026.
Data presentation: Additional interim results from the ongoing BB-301 Phase 1b/2a trial accepted for late-breaking presentation at the ESGCT Annual Congress, October 27–30, 2026 in Hamburg.
Pivotal planning: Company anticipates initiating the BB-301 pivotal trial in mid-2027, aiming to advance the candidate for OPMD-related dysphagia.

Program description: BB-301 is a locally administered AAV9-based "silence and replace" construct combining codon-optimized PABPN1 replacement with two siRNAs targeting mutant PABPN1; it holds Orphan and Fast Track designations from regulators.

title: Benitec Biopharma reports FY2026 net loss $45.5M, cash $180.0M; advances BB-301 clinical program
